title: Drinking and dissipation among musicians
summary: Stewart on musicians' excess, groove juice, Tatum's heavy drinking that did not affect his playing, and Garner being cooler.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Now, did you find that the -- what did you think about the degree of dissipation that a lot of the guys were into in those years because, you know, in all of the different generations of jazz players so far, a lot of guys have been killed off by, you know, excess.

Yes. Well, I didn't dwell on that too much, about the different fellows. Of course, when you speak of dissipation and what have you, I imagine we all had our little things going for us that weren't too kosher. When you take a look at Charlie Parker, you can't say that was the cause of him going by the wayside or what have you. But anyway, the vices of different ones, it probably wasn't too good for the [cross talk].
What about Jimmy Blanton? What was he like? Did he dissipate?
I don't know for sure about Jimmy. I didn't know too well about his dissipation or what have you.
When you were around him though, he didn't --
Oh, no, right.
I don't mean drugs. I didn't mean drugs.
Yeah.
I meant like whether he drank a lot.
Drank, yeah, right.
And stayed up all --
I imagine we all had our moments, being young, you know, where we put away quite a -- what Slim and I used to call it, groove juice, you know.
(Laughter.)
And what I mean, drinking was -- we could at least take it moreso than we could as we grew older, you know. But a lot of it was overdone, sure.
Why do you think the guys dissipate -- well, you know, like drank to such excesses?
Yes, well --
Do you have any idea why guys did that?

I don't have any idea. At times, I used to put away a bit, you know. But I wouldn't call -- never call myself an alcoholic, you know. But there were times when I called myself keeping up with -- say, for instance, Art Tatum. He used to put it away quite a bit, you know, like
he used to drink Seagrams Seven with a beer chaser. (Laughter.) You know? And he used to put it away quite a bit and sometimes I would call myself trying to keep up with him, you know.
Did it affect his playing?
No.
He played just as well --
Just as well. That's the way it seemed to me, sure.
What about Garner?
Garner? I don't think he was too much of a boozer, what I mean? I think Garner was a little more cool, yes.
Yeah, because I know like Lawrence Brown didn't do anything.
Right.
That's what Sonny Greer told me, he was -- in fact, they called him Deacon.
Yeah. Oh, yeah, there you go.
Because he was a teetotaler. They said he was a heavy ladies' man.
Yeah.
